chapters.summary: Moved by God, Cyrus king of Persia issues a decree allowing the exiled people of Judah to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple, and he restores the temple vessels to them.
keyPoints: God stirs the heart of King Cyrus to issue a decree permitting the people of Judah to return, fulfilling the word of the prophet.
The heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, together with the priests and Levites, respond to the call and prepare to return to Jerusalem.
Their neighbors support those returning with silver, gold, goods, livestock, and freewill offerings, and the vessels of the temple are also brought back.
chapters.application: God can move human hearts to accomplish his purposes; let us submit to his leading, give willingly, and take part in the work of spiritual rebuilding.

chapters.summary: This chapter records in detail the names and numbers of those who returned from exile, emphasizing God's faithfulness and restoration toward his people.
keyPoints: The families and numbers of those who returned are recorded, showing that God's promise is fulfilled.
Priests, Levites, Nethinims, and others return, each according to his own calling.
Those who return have their identity confirmed by genealogy, safeguarding the purity of temple service.
chapters.application: God numbers his people one by one; let us likewise treasure our identity in God's household and serve him with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: The Israelites who have returned from exile rebuild the altar in Jerusalem and begin offering sacrifices to God, laying the foundation for rebuilding the temple.
keyPoints: The people of Israel gather together in Jerusalem as one man, preparing to rebuild the temple.
They first rebuild the altar and restore the morning and evening burnt offerings, worshiping God.
Though afraid of the surrounding peoples, they still persist in offering sacrifices and begin gathering materials to rebuild the temple.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us first restore our worship of God and act together in unity, for he will surely grant peace and guidance.

chapters.summary: Ezra chapter 4 records how the enemies of Judah and Benjamin obstructed the rebuilding of the temple, so that the work was halted until the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia.
keyPoints: The enemies of Judah pretend to want to help build the temple, but Zerubbabel refuses them.
The enemies write letters accusing the Jews, misleading the Persian king into ordering the work stopped.
The work of rebuilding the temple is forced to a halt, until the second year of King Darius.
chapters.application: When we face opposition and obstacles, let us hold fast to faith, wait patiently for God's leading, and trust that his purposes will surely be accomplished.

chapters.summary: Encouraged by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel and Jeshua resume the rebuilding of the temple and face questioning from the Persian governor.
keyPoints: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah, in the name of God, urge the people to continue building the temple.
Zerubbabel and Jeshua lead the people to resume the work, and God is with them.
The governor beyond the river reports to King Darius, but the eye of God watches over the elders of Judah.
chapters.application: When our work is hindered, let us listen to God's word, be strong in the Lord, and continue on to complete our mission. God will surely watch over us and bring his purpose to pass.

chapters.summary: King Darius discovers the decree of King Cyrus and permits the Jews to continue rebuilding the temple; the temple is finally completed and dedicated, and the Passover is celebrated.
keyPoints: King Darius searches the archives, confirms the decree of King Cyrus, and supports the rebuilding of the temple.
The governor beyond the river obeys the command and supplies all that is needed, and the work on the temple is completed successfully.
The people of Israel dedicate the temple and keep the Passover with great joy and gladness.
chapters.application: When things seem to be at a standstill, let us trust that God is sovereign over all and will surely fulfill his promises. Let us be faithful in our duties and worship him with thankful hearts.

chapters.summary: Ezra leads a second group of exiles back to Jerusalem, receives a decree of support from King Artaxerxes, and reaffirms the law, displaying God's faithfulness and grace.
keyPoints: Ezra, a descendant of Aaron and well versed in the law, receives God's favor and the king's permission to go up to Jerusalem.
King Artaxerxes issues a decree permitting Ezra to bring silver, gold, and offerings back to Jerusalem, and commands that all his needs be supplied.
Ezra sets his heart to study and obey the law of the LORD, and to teach its statutes and ordinances to Israel.
chapters.application: Let us follow Ezra's example, devoting ourselves to studying God's word and gladly obeying it, while relying on the hand of God to become a channel of blessing wherever we are.

chapters.summary: Ezra leads a group of exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem; along the way they fast and pray for God's protection, and Ezra faithfully delivers the temple's silver and gold.
keyPoints: Ezra gathers the Levites and the people by genealogy, preparing them for the return.
At the river Ahava he proclaims a fast, asking God for a safe journey.
He weighs out the silver, gold, and vessels and entrusts them to the priests, and after arriving they offer burnt offerings.
chapters.application: Before making important decisions, let us follow Ezra's example, seeking God through prayer and fasting, trusting in his protection, and faithfully managing all that he has entrusted to us.

chapters.summary: Ezra learns that the people of Israel have intermarried with the surrounding peoples and adopted their detestable practices; grief-stricken, he confesses their sin and prays to God for forgiveness.
keyPoints: Ezra hears that the people have intermarried with the surrounding nations and followed their detestable practices, and he is deeply grieved.
He tears his garment and his cloak, pulls hair from his head and beard, and sits appalled, fasting and weeping before God over the people's sin.
Ezra prays and confesses to God, acknowledging that the people's guilt is great, yet giving thanks that God in his grace has left them a remnant.
chapters.application: When we see sin around us, let us follow Ezra's example, first humbly confessing it, and asking God to cleanse us and keep us living holy lives.

chapters.summary: Ezra leads the people in confession and repentance, dealing with the problem of intermarriage with the surrounding peoples, and restoring the purity of the covenant.
keyPoints: The people have sinned by marrying foreign women; Ezra weeps bitterly and confesses, and all the people weep with him.
Ezra calls the people to confess to God and make a covenant to put away their foreign wives and separate from them.
The whole assembly gathers to deal with the matter, examining it family by family, and it takes three months to complete.
chapters.application: When we stray from God, let us be bold to confess our sin and take action to make it right. May the Lord give us a repentant heart and restore our relationship with him.
